The command's output never reaches an event, a log line, a refusal message, lazyslice.yml or the trace; its own stderr passes through to the operator untouched
A command that exits non-zero, times out or prints nothing refuses the run with a message naming the exit status and nothing else
The command also runs for an endpoint the discovery ladder resolved, not only for one named on the command line

f7b5f56.title: README, SECURITY, CONCEPT, the quickstart transcript and the launch drafts describe what v0.4.0 does
bullets: README, SECURITY.md and CONCEPT.md now describe v0.4.0's actual behaviour: JSON columns mask leaf by leaf (free text still masks whole; CONCEPT.md no longer says both are masked whole), the neighbouring-column rule promotes low to possible confidence, a bare name/display_name/<x>_name column needs corroboration before a name hit alone masks it, and a hex token exactly a digest's length is spared and copied beside a certain personal neighbour.

The quickstart run excerpt in README and docs/QUICKSTART_TRANSCRIPT.md now shows the classify.summary and plan.summary lines a run with no committed lazyslice.yml prints (`N column(s): ... masked, ... copied, ... never-masked keys` and `N table(s) reached, ... unreachable, ... rows`), and the root-table prompt example now reads `root table? [public.customers]`.

The exit-code table and the --mask/--unmask reference in README now match current behaviour: exit 2 for the same-database refusal is described as the target gate's first (identity) rule, exit 5 covers a target credential too, exit 7 covers a failed row-count/sequence check, exit 9 covers an unmasked column that validates as personal data, and the `--mask` flag a second-net refusal names when no other category fits the column's type is `--mask TABLE.COL=special_category`, the one category every type accepts.

README's 'What a snapshot will not hide' section states two limits that were previously undocumented on the front page: the residual scan tests canonical equality only, and a snapshot should be regenerated (and the masking key rotated) after an erasure request.

SECURITY.md's known-limitations list now orders item 2 (bare national identifier) and item 4 (general unrecognised shape) the way README and THREAT_MODEL.md already do, and folds in the card-number column-name-suffix wording, the enumeration/identifier-shape and hex-digest residuals, and the one-case/prefixed/colon-separated hex forms the entropy check now spares.

The launch drafts under docs/launch/ no longer call masking a 'keyed hash': the Reddit drafts describe deterministic fakes under a local key, and the web-development draft says a first run at a terminal asks only what it cannot settle itself (which table to start from and, when no target is found, whether to start one) rather than at most one question.

README's quickstart section and docs/QUICKSTART_TRANSCRIPT.md now explain the full_name column's address-shaped output: the column name says person_name, but its sample values (which carry a trailing digit in this schema) read as addresses, and when the name and the values disagree about the category the values decide. README's Census-names sentence now says it applies to a column masked under person_name, not to this full_name example.

306f25e.title: README and SECURITY residual 4 name the two shapes a version-named or key-named column now copies
bullets: README.md's list of accepted residuals now names two more unmasked shapes under residual 4: IP/MAC addresses appearing as a minority of a version/build/release column's values, and a guessed-region phone number under a key/code/license/serial/token column name when the table's best personal neighbour is only likely rather than certain.
SECURITY.md's known-limitations item 4 names the same two cases.

THREAT_MODEL.md's T-0317 amendment states that no corpus-wide before/after classify --json comparison over the ten torture schemas was run for this change, so the two truth-set numbers it quotes are not a corpus-wide measurement.

b1060f8.title: THREAT_MODEL.md T1 carries the amendment for the version-column network veto and the key/code/license/serial/token phone-guess veto
bullets: THREAT_MODEL.md's T1 threat now documents the T-0317 classifier change: a column whose name carries version, build or release as a word is no longer offered the network-address (IP/MAC) signal as a minority-value hit, and a column whose name carries key, code, license, serial or token as a word is no longer offered the guessed-region phone corroboration.

The amendment names the personal data that change leaves unmasked (a minority of real IP/MAC addresses in a version/build/release-named column, and real non-configured-region phone numbers in a key/code/license/serial/token-named column beside only a 'likely' personal neighbour) as a widening of the fourth accepted residual README.md and SECURITY.md list.

3348bde.title: README and SECURITY say the card signal wants an issuer prefix, and what a card outside the issuer table costs
bullets: README.md's 'How it decides' now states the Luhn card check also requires a known issuer prefix, and under an id/number/version/reference column name, that issuer's own length.
README.md's accepted residual 4 now names the gap: a card number outside the issuer table's ranges, or of an unlisted length under such a column name, is copied.
SECURITY.md's known-limitations item 4 states the same bound: a card from a range the table lacks, or of an unlisted length under an identifier-shaped column name, is copied.

7a2a32d.title: README and SECURITY residual lists name the shapes the entropy check no longer reads as secrets
bullets: README.md's and SECURITY.md's residual lists now spell out the four shapes the entropy check passes through, copied unmasked, when no credential-name rule matches the column's name: a secret that is an exact 32/40/64-character hex run, a secret held in a column of one to four non-NULL rows, a secret in a column literally named type, klass or component_name, and a file named after a person in a column where fewer than a fifth of the file names carry a word the dictionary holds.

d66ab4c.title: A committed yml pins which document keys are copied, and a key the samples newly show counts as drift
bullets: lazyslice.yml now lists, under a json or jsonb column's new leaf_keys: entry, the document keys whose values the run copied, so the committed file shows which keys cross in clear (a yml format change for this 0.x minor; older lazyslice versions refuse a file carrying the key)

On a re-run from a committed lazyslice.yml, a document key the source now shows that the file does not list has every value under it masked instead of copied, and is printed as drift naming the column and the key (for example prefs->'guest'), never a value; the line ends 'masked, not copied until the key is listed under the column's leaf_keys:'
Such a key stays masked and reported as drift on every run until you add it to the column's leaf_keys: by hand: a run carries an existing list forward as it stands and never adds to it
--strict-schema now exits 10 when a document key is not listed in the committed yml, not only when a whole column is new, and the re-run summary's drift count includes such keys

A key that is not shaped like a field name is written to lazyslice.yml and named in drift lines as a sha256: fingerprint, not as itself: a name with a space, a UUID, a dotted handle, a key with digits other than a one- or two-digit suffix, a key of eight or more letters that are all hexadecimal, a key over 32 bytes, and every key of a column whose documents show more than 64 distinct keys; a word-shaped key that is itself personal (a username used as a key, in a column of few keys) is written as it stands
README, SECURITY.md item 8, THREAT_MODEL T1/T3/T5 and ARCHITECTURE describe leaf_keys: and key drift

A lazyslice.yml written before this release lists no leaf keys: the first run over it masks every value under the document keys it would otherwise copy, reports each key once as drift and writes the list into the file, and later runs copy them; with --strict-schema that drift is exit 10, so a pipeline that runs with the flag must run once without it to write the list before the strict run passes again

4a78cb3.title: A lazyslice.yml written by v0.3.0 still finds its lazyslice-target-lazyslice-* container after the container name rule changed
bullets: A lazyslice.yml whose target was recorded as lazyslice-target-lazyslice-<something>, the name v0.3.0 gave the container of a directory called lazyslice-<something>, is still recognised as this directory's own container, and the password remembered for it is still read, so a second run from that directory connects without a password being given

ARCHITECTURE.md section 9 records that the container name lazyslice-target-<project> is not a one-to-one function of the project name (shop and lazyslice-shop share one), and which checks stop one directory from taking another's container: --create-target's own-container check and the start-a-container question's reuse check

6896570.title: The screens' exit keys: esc closes help, enter asks before a run that writes, ctrl+c exits 130
bullets: --tui: pressing esc while the help overlay ("?") is open now closes the overlay and returns to the screen, instead of quitting the whole program.

--tui: pressing enter on a run or verify screen (the two that would drop and rewrite the target) now shows a one-line confirmation naming the target, the table and row counts, and the flags the screens set, and needs a second enter to actually start the run; enter on the classify or plan screens is unchanged since neither writes anywhere.
--tui: any key other than enter or ctrl+c dismisses that confirmation and returns to the screen with nothing changed and nothing run; ctrl+c there exits 130.
--tui with --plan asks for no confirmation, since a plan-only run never writes anything.
--tui: ctrl+c now exits 130 (the documented interrupt code), matching a SIGINT during the run itself, instead of exiting 0 like a plain esc or "q".

--tui: leaving the screens without running (esc, "q", or ctrl+c) no longer prints a truncated copy of the plan or classification table into scrollback; it prints one line instead: on a run or verify screen, "stopped before writing anything; nothing changed in <target>", naming the real target endpoint, and on a classify or plan screen, or with --plan, the plain "stopped before writing anything", naming no target.

--tui: pressing ctrl+c while answering an unmask reason or a take/depth/cap prompt now exits as an interrupt (exit 130), the same as ctrl+c on every other screen, instead of only discarding the typed answer.

23d619e.title: --create-target's container name no longer doubles the prefix for a directory named lazyslice-*
bullets: Running lazyslice --create-target from a directory already named lazyslice-<something> (or with a compose project name starting lazyslice- or lazyslice_) now creates/looks for lazyslice-target-<something>, not the doubled lazyslice-target-lazyslice-<something>.

--create-target now refuses at exit 4 with target.refused.name_taken ("a container named ... already exists and lazyslice did not create it for this directory", naming --target) when the container it would create or reuse belongs to a different project or directory, instead of silently adopting, starting, and loading into whatever container already held that name.

8fbae37.title: Discovery chooses the empty target container lazyslice itself created, and no longer offers to start a duplicate on the next port
bullets: A second run from the directory whose first run created lazyslice-target-<project> now loads into that container without asking, including headless with no --yes; it no longer asks 'no local postgres found... start one?' for the same name on the next port or stops at exit 4 target.refused.none

The container lazyslice created for this directory is chosen as the target when it is empty or carries lazyslice's marker, even though its database is named postgres; every other container's postgres, template0 and template1 databases are still never picked as a target

The start-a-container question is never asked for a container name that already exists: a stopped container of that name that lazyslice created for this directory gets the 'is stopped — start it?' question, and a running one is reused with no question

New exit-4 refusal target.refused.name_taken: when the lazyslice-target-<project> name is already held by a container lazyslice did not create for this directory, the run names the container and --target, at a terminal as well as headless, and does not read, start, reuse or write to that container

Discovery no longer takes over the lazyslice-target container that a second checkout or worktree with the same folder name created: when no target is named, a run only reuses, without asking, a container whose recorded working directory is the current one; a target recorded in a committed lazyslice.yml is still found by its container name from any directory

c27caf6.title: A committed yml whose target is a container lazyslice created reconnects or re-provisions, and says which
bullets: A committed lazyslice.yml whose target is a container lazyslice created now works from any directory: the run finds the container by name and connects with the password from the container's own environment, instead of failing with a raw 'password authentication failed (SQLSTATE 28P01)'.

When the committed target container no longer exists (another machine, or it was removed), a run at a terminal is offered a new container in the question, or goes to this directory's own lazyslice-target-<project> when that already exists, and a headless run stops at exit 4 with target.refused.container_missing naming the container, --create-target and --target.

When the committed target container is stopped, the run starts it (asking 'is stopped — start it?' at a terminal, without asking headless) and loads into the database the file records, the same database it uses when the container is already running.
--create-target now overrides a committed target that names a lazyslice container: it creates or reuses this directory's own lazyslice-target-<project>, with no question asked.

A target that answers and rejects the password now stops at exit 4 with target.refused.auth, naming the endpoint, the role, and every place a password can come from (--target, $PGPASSWORD, ~/.pgpass, --password-command), instead of saying the target did not respond.

The not-empty target refusal now reads 'the target <db> is not empty (<tables>): <reason>' with every placeholder filled; when the target holds lazyslice's copy of a different source it says so, and it names --target as the way through. docs/ERRORS.md lists the two new codes and the changed row.

a70e717.title: A stray positional argument is a usage error at exit 2; the root command takes its source only from --source
bullets: The root command no longer accepts a positional argument at all, so the source is passed with --source and `lazyslice postgres://...` exits 2; `lazyslice --source DSN --create-target ' --unmask x'` (one unsplit shell variable) now exits 2 naming the stray argument instead of exiting 4 with a confusing 'no local postgres found' / 'server version' message.

The usage error for a stray positional argument never echoes a password: an argument that looks like a connection string (contains '=', '@', ':' or '/') is named without its own text beyond the role, host, port and database ('a connection string (role@host:port/db)' when it parses, or a generic phrase when it doesn't), regardless of scheme case or whether it's a URI or a libpq keyword/value string; an argument with none of those characters (a genuine shell-quoting mistake) is quoted in full so the mistake stays visible.

A subcommand (plan, introspect, classify, verify, doctor) that receives both --source and a positional DSN now refuses at exit 2 naming the extra argument, instead of silently overwriting the --source value and reporting a confusing 'bad --source' error later.
ARCHITECTURE.md shows `lazyslice --source DSN` in place of `lazyslice [DSN]`; the subcommands still take a positional DSN.

849dd90.title: --unmask on a first run reports no drift against a file that does not exist; the drift message names the real decision
bullets: A run using only the --unmask flags with no committed lazyslice.yml in the directory no longer prints a classify.column.drift warning for every column the flags did not name; drift is now only ever reported against a committed file that actually exists, matching a run with no --unmask flag at all.

The --strict-schema flag on a first run with --unmask flags no longer risks a false exit code 10 over columns the flags did not mention; it now fires only against a committed yml, when that file omits a column or a document key.

The classify.column.drift warning now states what actually happened to the column instead of a fixed phrase: copied, or masked as its category, rather than always printing masked at or above possible even for a column that was in fact copied unmasked, such as a boolean column below the mask threshold.

cb223fa.title: The reasons dump and the plan end with a summary, and a re-run from a committed yml is quiet
bullets: A fresh run's per-column masking reasons now end with one summary line: "N column(s): A masked, B copied, C never-masked keys" (classify.summary), instead of scrolling off with no count.

A re-run from a committed lazyslice.yml no longer reprints the reason of every column the file already settles: it prints the reason lines of columns the file has not seen, columns this run decided differently and columns holding a document key the file does not list, the drift and opt-out-expiry warnings, and one line "N decisions from PATH, D drift, C changed" (classify.reused) in place of the rest; changed counts the columns the yml recorded a decision for that this run decided differently (new sampled evidence, a new --mask/--unmask flag, or a new pattern), kept separate from drift, which counts what the yml never saw at all.
The plan's per-table listing now ends with one summary line: "T table(s) reached, U unreachable, R rows" (plan.summary), instead of leaving a reader to count schema_only lines by hand.
--json/NDJSON output carries the same new classify.summary, classify.reused and plan.summary events as the human-readable transcript.

Only the plain-text transcript is folded: on a re-run from a committed lazyslice.yml the --tui reasons screen and the --json event stream still receive every column's classify.masked.column/classify.copied.column event.

1f4a02e.title: A green run prints one verify summary line and how to reach the target
bullets: A successful run now ends with a `verify:` line summarizing every check it ran: foreign keys validated, table row counts matched (with total rows), the residual scan's outcome, and how many columns the second net scanned.
A successful run also prints a line beginning `target` that names the database, host, port and role of the database it just wrote, and where the password lives — never the password itself.

For a target running in a Docker container (whether found by discovery or started with --create-target), that line gives a ready-to-run `docker exec <container> printenv POSTGRES_PASSWORD` instead of leaving the operator to `docker inspect` it themselves.
For any other target, it names --password-command when that flag supplied the password, or points at the connection string / $PGPASSWORD / ~/.pgpass otherwise.

Both new lines are also emitted as `--json` events (`verify.summary`, `target.connect`, `target.connect.container`, `target.connect.password_command`), consistent with every other line in the transcript.
docs/ERRORS.md lists the four new event codes.

7326e8a.title: --mask masks a copied column; every second-net failure reported at once
bullets: When the post-load check finds several copied columns that still look like personal data, the run now names every one of them, each on its own verify.refused.second_net line (or one of that code's document and type-conflict variants), before exiting 9, instead of one column per run

New --mask TABLE.COL[=CATEGORY] flag masks a column the classifier copied, as free_text or as the category named, with no reason required; it is recorded in lazyslice.yml under the column's new mask: block, with the category the column was actually masked as and by: flag, and later runs keep masking it with no flag

The verify.refused.second_net message now says how to fix it: --mask TABLE.COL=CATEGORY with the category the check found, or --skip-table TABLE, so --unmask is no longer the only way to a passing run

A --mask, or a mask: entry in lazyslice.yml, on a column that cannot be masked, such as a surrogate key or generated column or a type the category does not fit, exits 2 with the new classify.refused.mask message naming every such column; it is never copied quietly

A --mask on a column the classifier already masks under another category, or that comes out under a category other than the one named, is exit 2 naming that category, so the flag never quietly swaps a masker
Passing --mask and --unmask for the same column, a category that does not exist, or one column with two different categories is exit 2 before anything connects
With --tui, adding an --unmask on the review screens no longer makes the second run drop --phone-region when it checks the classification the operator reviewed, and --mask is carried the same way

7eacaf8.title: A lookup step shows the rows it will copy, not 0 rows
bullets: A lookup step (a small reference table like country, which other tables reference and which references nothing itself) no longer shows "0 rows" on its plan line or on the --tui plan screen; it shows the number of rows that table will copy.
An ordinary lookup table's plan reason reads "copied whole" instead of the bare word "lookup".

A framework metadata table (e.g. Rails schema_migrations) over 1,000 rows reports 1,000 rows on its plan line and in the overall estimate, the same figure as the reason beside it, which says only the first 1,000 rows (ordered by identity) are copied.

8e2177c.title: the second_net hint names a --mask category the column's type accepts, or semi_structured for a json column
bullets: A second-net refusal on an unmasked json, jsonb or hstore column has its own code, verify.refused.second_net_document (exit 9), and hints --mask TABLE.COL=semi_structured, whatever category matched a leaf.

A second-net refusal on an already-masked json, jsonb or hstore column (verify.refused.second_net_document_masked, exit 9) says the column is already masked and offers --skip-table TABLE alone, because --mask cannot change a masked column's category.

A second-net refusal whose matched category the column's own type does not accept (verify.refused.second_net_type_conflict, exit 9: a network_id hit on a uuid column, for example) hints `--mask TABLE.COL=special_category`, the one category every type accepts.
Every other second-net refusal keeps the verify.refused.second_net code, whose hint names --mask TABLE.COL=CATEGORY with the category the check found.
docs/ERRORS.md has a row for each of the three new error codes.

1ff4986.title: A --mask or lazyslice.yml raise on a key column also masks the columns that reference it
bullets: --mask on a key column, or a mask: block naming one, also masks every column that references it by foreign key, under the same category, so the join holds in the copy; that includes a uuid or integer foreign-key column, which is otherwise exempt from masking as a key
A lazyslice.yml pattern or column entry that raises a key column now carries through to the columns that reference it, the way a key the classifier masks itself always has
A column with its own --unmask or unmask: entry is still copied as it is when the key it references is masked

A column that references a key masked with --mask or a mask: block, but whose type cannot take the key's category (for example a citext child of a key masked as person_date), stops the run at exit 2 (classify.refused.mask) before any write, naming the child for a --mask of its own; it is not copied in clear.
README's --mask section says that masking a key also masks the columns that reference it

3222140.title: The second net exempts the same columns from the entropy check as the classifier: type, klass and component_name, not '_type', and never a document's leaves
bullets: The second net's exemption from the entropy check covers exactly the column names the classifier's does: `type`, `klass` and `component_name`. A column named `_type` is exempt in neither: the classifier and the second net both put its values to the entropy check.

The second net scans the string leaves of a jsonb, json or hstore column named `type`, `klass` or `component_name` for credential-shaped values; only the column's own scalar value is exempt, matching the classifier's document-leaf path.

6e835ad.title: The neighbouring-column rule spares a hex column only at a digest's length, so a column of hex tokens of 13 to 31 characters is still masked
bullets: A column of hex tokens of 13 to 31 characters (API keys, reset tokens, invite codes, session ids) under a neutral name next to a certain email or IP column is still masked, as in v0.3.0; it is not spared as 'hex digests'

The neighbouring-column rule skips a hex column only when its values have a digest's length: 8 to 12 characters (an abbreviated commit hash), or exactly 32, 40, 64 or 128 characters when the value does not also look like a secret
THREAT_MODEL.md T1 states what this skip leaves: a hex token of exactly a digest's length, under a neutral column name, is copied unmasked

401a1fe.title: The plan reports every refusal in one run, and a no-identity hint names the columns
bullets: A plan refusal (no row identity, a masked column its type can't hold, --skip-table on a needed parent, or a masked column under a unique index too narrow to widen) no longer stops the run at the first cause found: `lazyslice plan` (and any writing run) now reports every independent cause it can find in one pass, each as its own line, still exiting 12.

The "has no row identity" refusal's `--key` hint now names the table's own columns (e.g. `--key public.line_items_products=order_id,product_id`) instead of the generic `--key TABLE=col,col` placeholder, for a table of three columns or fewer whose columns are all NOT NULL and of a type the tool can compare. A table with a nullable column, or a json, xml or geometric column, keeps the generic placeholder.
When the pseudo-key probe has already found those columns non-unique, the hint offers --skip-table alone, because a --key naming them would be refused as not unique on the next run.

A schema with several independent plan-time refusals can now take a fraction of a second longer to refuse, because finding a unique-index collision in the same pass needs the walk to run even after an earlier cause (a table with no identity, an unwritable column) was already found; the process still exits 12 exactly once.

4679f75.title: a version column is not an IP address and a digit-only license key is not a phone number
bullets: A column whose name carries version, build or release (app_version, app_build_number) is no longer masked as free text because a minority of its dotted-integer values parse as IPv4 addresses; a column whose values genuinely are addresses is still masked as network_id.

A column whose name carries key, code, license, serial or token is never masked as phone by the guessed-region corroboration, even when its digits clear a guessed numbering plan beside a personal neighbour; it can still be masked as free text by the ordinary sweep when it is signal-less beside a certain column.

The leak check agrees: verify's second net does not ask the IP or MAC address question of a version, build or release column, so a copied one does not stop the run at exit 9 over the same dotted values.

369b39a.title: The Luhn check needs a card length and issuer prefix before it masks an id, number or version column
bullets: A column of customer, subscription, invoice or estimate numbers, or a migration version, is no longer masked as free text because one value passes the card checksum by chance: a card number must now also start with a known card issuer's prefix

In a column whose name ends in id, number, num, no, nr, version, ref or reference, a value counts as a card only when its length is one its issuer uses, so a 14-digit migration timestamp is copied and not masked
The post-load check (exit 9) uses the same card rule as the classifier, so it does not refuse a loaded copy over an identifier column the classifier left unmasked on purpose

A card number with a known issuer's prefix is still masked, whether written plain, grouped with spaces or dashes, or dotted; under a column name ending in id, number, num, no, nr, version, ref or reference its length must also be one that issuer uses. A card whose prefix is in no issuer range, or whose length its issuer does not use under such a name, is not recognised as a card and is copied when nothing else masks its column (README residual 4, SECURITY.md item 4)

7749cc9.title: The entropy validator does not read filenames, hex digests, namespaced class names or a handful of samples as secrets
bullets: File names (exported reports, logos, screenshots, media files, software releases, webcam shots) are no longer read as secrets and masked as credentials to the fixed $lazyslice$invalid value. A file name whose part before the extension contains a word from the name dictionary still counts as one; a value with a file extension is judged by this rule alone, so a file name that carries a person's name, such as '<surname>_<givenname>_1906_birth_cert.pdf', is not spared as a dotted class name

MD5, SHA-1 and SHA-256 digests (32, 40 or 64 hex characters in one case, bare, after an md5:, sha1: or sha256: prefix, or written as colon-separated byte pairs) are no longer read as secrets; a hex token of 32 characters or more at any other length, or in mixed case, still is

Rails single-table-inheritance class names are copied unchanged instead of becoming $lazyslice$invalid, which raised on every row the application loaded: this covers columns named type, klass or component_name, class names namespaced with ::, dotted class names in which a segment is camelCase and no word is a dictionary name, and environment-variable names such as AWS_S3_BUCKET_V2 (at most two digits per word and no dictionary name)

A column with fewer than five sampled values is no longer masked as a credential just because its values look random; a column whose name says it is a credential is still masked on the name, and the post-load second net applies the same five-value floor, so it does not refuse such a column at exit 9

A column of file names in which at least a fifth name a person (for example photo-<username>-3.jpg) is still masked whole, with the reason 'N/N samples are file names, a fifth or more carrying a dictionary name'
Columns named key_hash (a hash of an API key) are now masked as credentials by name, because their hex values are no longer read as secrets

Values that only resemble those shapes stay with the entropy check, as in v0.3.0: a dotted handle such as '<givenname>.<surname>84', an upper-case value built from a name and a year such as 'DUBLIN_<GIVENNAME>_<SURNAME>_1906', and an all-lowercase dotted module path such as 'billing.invoice_mailer.v2', which is still masked as a credential as the stated price of keeping dotted handles masked

Other secrets stay masked as before: API keys, access tokens, JWTs, bcrypt/argon2/pbkdf2 password hashes and OAuth client secrets. What the entropy check now passes through, in a column no credential name rule matches, is a secret that is a one-case hex run of exactly 32, 40 or 64 characters, a secret column of one to four non-NULL rows, a secret in a column named type, klass or component_name, and a file named after a person in a column where fewer than a fifth of the file names carry a dictionary name (README residual 4, SECURITY.md item 4)

9eef352.title: A bare 'name' column and a '*_file_name' column are not a person's name without corroboration
bullets: A column called just `name`, `display_name` or `<thing>_name` in a table not named for people (tags, folders, roles, languages, AI models, plans) is now copied when its samples carry no names from the name dictionary, instead of being masked as a person's name and refusing the plan under a unique index

A bare `name` column is still masked when its table or its own name contains a word for people (`users.name`, `staff.display_name`, `orders.customer_name`), when at least a fifth of its samples hold a name the dictionary knows, when it has fewer than three sampled values, or when a column beside it is decided personal at `likely` or above (a neighbour masked on its name alone, such as a `phone` column, does not count)

The words for people include clients, players, drivers, agents, tenants, landlords, workers, artists, speakers, actors, holders, sellers, riders, parents, mothers and fathers: a bare `name` column in a table so named is masked without checking its values

A column whose own qualifier names a person (legal_name, preferred_name, nick_name, married_name, billing_name, shipping_name, card_holder_name, name_on_card, name_given, name_family and similar) is still masked on its name alone, in any table, even when its values are names the dictionary does not know
Columns ending in `_file_name` (Paperclip's `logo_file_name`, `image_file_name`, `dump_file_name`) are no longer treated as a person's name

`lazyslice classify` reason lines now say why a bare name was masked or copied: which word for people corroborated it, how many samples carried a dictionary name, or that too few samples were available to check
A device name built on its owner's name in a possessive, such as "<givenname>'s iPhone", now counts as carrying that name, so such a column stays masked

README.md and SECURITY.md's third accepted residual now says that a bare `name` column of a non-person table, holding names the dictionary does not carry (for example a non-Latin script), is copied, and that a neighbouring column protects it only when that neighbour is decided at `likely` or above

c9c0f68.title: The same-column-name rule does not propagate a decision that was itself only a neighbour sweep
bullets: A decision the neighbouring-column sweep reached on no name or value signal of its own (only a certain neighbour sitting beside it, e.g. an unrecognised uuid/state/filename/colour column beside an email column) is no longer copied onto a same-named column in an unrelated table via the same-column-name rule; that same-named column is masked only when it has real evidence of its own, or when another column with real evidence shares its name. A column v0.3.0 masked only on that inheritance is therefore copied unless something else raises it, which ARCHITECTURE.md's amendment records as a recall change against THREAT_MODEL.md T1.

A swept column that foreign-key propagation then confirmed with real evidence remains a source for the same-column-name rule, so a same-named column in an unrelated table inherits that category (e.g. email).

d0b41b3.title: The neighbouring-column sweep spares enum-like and identifier-shaped columns, and says why a column was not swept
bullets: A text column sitting beside a certain email, phone or IP column is no longer filled with free-text filler when its sampled values are an enumeration: at least 10 samples, at most 20 distinct values, each seen at least twice. Columns like role, state and log_level are now copied, so a copied Rails database boots.
A text column whose every sampled value is a UUID, hex digest, semantic version, hostname or path is copied instead of being swept into free-text masking beside a personal column.

Each column spared this way gets a reason line starting 'not swept by the neighbouring-column rule' that says why: enum-like with its counts, the identifier shape it matched, or its unique index. The unique-index skip used to be silent.

A value that carries a dictionary name or a special-category term, or that is a gender or title term (male, female, mrs), is never spared. Neither is a non-ASCII value in an enumeration, an enumeration with fewer than 10 samples or an identifier shape with fewer than 3, so a repeated native-script name or a /home/<name> path is still masked.

Blood groups, marital status, ISO dates, CamelCase handles built from a given name and a surname, and runs of four or more digits, alone or joined by hyphens, dots, slashes or a plus sign (postcodes, ZIP+4 codes, local phone numbers), are not spared as enumerations: beside a certain personal column they are still masked.
A column of dates of birth written as unpadded dotted dates (5.3.1985) or with a month name (05/Mar/1985), beside a certain personal column, is still masked: it is not spared as versions or paths.

A bare home directory such as /home/<username>, or a two-segment route, is not spared as a path. A value counts as a path only if it has a file extension, is an absolute path with three or more segments, or is a time zone name such as Europe/London.

A currency-code foreign-key pair beside a personal column, which used to refuse the run at exit 12 (plan.refused.unique_domain), now loads with both ends copied and still matching. A pair whose partner carries its own name signal still refuses at exit 12.
A project with a lazyslice.yml written by an earlier release keeps masking these columns until the file is regenerated with --reconfigure, because a committed yml can only tighten.

README's 'How it decides' section and residual 4 describe the spared shapes and what is never spared (blood groups, marital status, dates and postcode-length numbers). THREAT_MODEL T1 records the recall measurement and what can still be copied.

d0cf6c5.title: A migration tool's bookkeeping tables are copied whatever the walk reaches and their bookkeeping columns are not masked, so a Rails copy knows its migrations ran
bullets: Framework migration tables (schema_migrations, ar_internal_metadata, flyway_schema_history, django_migrations, alembic_version, knex_migrations, goose_db_version, __EFMigrationsHistory, atlas_schema_revisions, _prisma_migrations, SequelizeMeta, DATABASECHANGELOG and DATABASECHANGELOGLOCK) are copied into the target whatever the plan's walk reaches, whole when the table holds 1,000 rows or fewer; a schema_migrations table with no foreign key pointing at it used to be left empty, and a fresh Rails checkout re-ran every migration. A table with more than 1,000 rows is cut short by the lookup read's row bound, and its plan line says so: "has more than 1000 rows -- only the first 1000 (ordered by identity) are copied".

A migration tool's own bookkeeping columns (versions, checksums, timestamps, flags) are not masked on their names or values, and the leak check does not refuse a run over them: a migration timestamp that happens to pass the Luhn check is copied as it is. Such a column is still masked when a lazyslice.yml pattern or column entry raises it, or when it references a masked column by foreign key.
A framework table's identity-bearing columns (Flyway's installed_by, Liquibase's AUTHOR and LOCKEDBY) are not bookkeeping columns and are classified like any other column.
Rails' ar_internal_metadata has its environment row rewritten to development in the target, so a checkout of a snapshot is not refused a destructive rake task for still saying production.

The plan names a framework table on its own line: "framework metadata table, copied whole regardless of reachability", or the first-1000-rows sentence for a larger table, with "environment rewritten to development" added for ar_internal_metadata.

1851eb6.title: Personal values are recognised when written in fullwidth characters, with dash, underscore or slash separators, behind mailto: or sms:, percent-encoded or base64-encoded
bullets: An email, phone number, card or national identifier written in fullwidth characters (a fullwidth @, + or digits) is recognised and masked: in a plain text column, where v0.3.0 did not recognise it, and in a JSON value under a key no rule names

A card number grouped with en dashes, em dashes, minus signs, underscores or zero-width characters, and a US Social Security number grouped with en dashes, em dashes, minus signs, underscores or slashes, is now recognised and masked instead of being copied into the target

An email address whose domain ends in a trailing dot, or written behind mailto:, and a phone number written behind sms: with a ?body= after it, are now recognised as the address or number inside and masked; a number behind a bare tel: or sms: was already recognised

Percent-encoded values (user%40example.org, %2B44...), backslash-u escaped values and base64-encoded addresses and numbers are now decoded once and masked as the email or phone number they hold, not only by chance as credentials

A base64 value written the way a shell or Postgres writes it, with the input's trailing newline encoded or the output wrapped into 76-character lines, is now read as the address, phone number or card it decodes to
A date written with dashes or slashes (2026-09-24, 24/09/2026) is still copied: the new separator rules skip calendar dates, so no date column is newly masked as a national identifier

THREAT_MODEL's obfuscation amendment now lists the spellings covered and the ones still not: HTML entities, backslash-x escapes, homoglyphs NFKC does not fold, and a token inside a longer decoded string

e4e09cc.title: A json or jsonb number is read with every digit, so a card number stored as a json number is recognised and masked
bullets: A number leaf in a json or jsonb column is read with its exact digits, not through floating point, so a card number longer than about 16 digits stored as a json number (for example a 19-digit payment card number under a document key with no name signal) is recognised and masked

The classifier's samples, the masking pass and verify's scan of the target all read a json or jsonb column from its own text, the precision a domain over jsonb already had. A json[] or jsonb[] array column is not covered: a number leaf past 2^53 inside one is still rounded before any validator reads it, so a card number that long stored there as a number may not be recognised

44f93ed.title: A composite type holding a json, jsonb or hstore field is refused at plan, not classified over its record text
bullets: A composite column whose declared type holds a json, jsonb or hstore field (or a nested composite that does) is refused at plan with exit 12, whatever its sampled values look like, closing a leak where an email hidden inside a document field's own record-quoted text reached the target under a green run.

The exit-12 message for a masked composite column now names the offending field and its family (json, jsonb or hstore) as well as the composite type, when that is why the composite cannot be trusted, instead of only saying the type is a composite.

verify now runs a second, independent check for the same composite-document shape, refusing a copy that somehow reached the target holding one, under a new event code, verify.refused.composite_document, at exit 9 (docs/ERRORS.md has its row), while still honouring an operator's own --unmask for that column.

THREAT_MODEL.md's T1 entry on composites now names the document-field case explicitly, and the case that stays open: a nested composite with no document field of its own is still read only by whole-value validators over each field, so a personal value two levels down is caught only by chance.

4e156d1.title: A json or jsonb column in a log-shaped table is replaced whole with {}, for CamelCase, *_activity and *_trace table names too
bullets: A jsonb/json column in a log-shaped table (audit, log, history, event, activity, trace tables, including a CamelCase name like Prisma's default AuditLog and an all-caps or embedded-acronym plural such as EVENTs or user_LOGs) is collapsed to {} rather than walked leaf by leaf, which is what the plan's "replaced whole" reasons line says. For a CamelCase table and an *_activity or *_trace table this is new: v0.3.0 printed that reasons line and then walked the document, masking every leaf and keeping its keys.

4872e2e.title: A generated column built from json document fields is checked one value at a time, and the keys it reads are masked when its values are personal
bullets: A generated column that builds an email address, a phone number or a card number out of copied JSON document fields (for example `data->>'u' || '@' || data->>'h'`) does not reach the target in cleartext at exit 0: verify refuses it at exit 9 unless the value is exactly one of its own row's masked document fields.

When a generated column's sampled values are recognised as an email, phone number, card number or another personal value, the document keys its expression reads with -> or ->> are masked under that category, so the target rebuilds the column from masked values and the run is not refused.
Supabase's auth.identities.email (`lower(identity_data ->> 'email')`) loads at exit 0: it holds the email masker's own output, and verify checks that row by row.

The threat model and the architecture's list of stated false negatives describe what crosses: an assembled value that no validator recognises, and keys read through #> or #>> path operators, which are not masked at plan time. Verify still refuses such a value when a validator recognises it.

85036cb.title: The phone region reaches document keys and leaves, and a key whose sampled leaves are phone numbers masks them
bullets: A run with --phone-region no longer stops at exit 9 over a JSON document whose keys are national-format phone numbers such as 07911 123456; those keys are now masked like international ones, and the value under each is masked too

With no --phone-region, a JSON key that no name rule recognises and whose sampled values are national-format phone numbers has every value under it masked as a phone number, when the table holds another personal column or the document holds a personal key: the same evidence a plain column of such numbers needs

SECURITY.md item 8 now says that JSON keys holding national-format phone numbers are masked only under --phone-region, and that a key whose sampled values are phone numbers masks everything under it; THREAT_MODEL.md T1 records this and what stays open: with no --phone-region a national-format number used as a key survives, and one under an unnamed key with no personal column or key beside it is copied

5aa03f6.title: A document column whose own name is personal has every leaf masked, whatever category the name matched
bullets: A json or jsonb column whose own name marks it personal (full_name, home_address, passwords, date_of_birth, national_id, emails, notes, by_phone and the like) has every leaf masked; the leaf-by-leaf rule copies no leaf of such a column.

Each string leaf of such a document is masked under the category its column name matched: a jsonb emails column gets fake addresses, and by_phone, home_address, national_id and passwords get their own maskers. A name, date-of-birth or notes column gets free-text filler.

The second net agrees with the rule: it does not refuse at exit 9 over the email, phone, address, national-id or credential masker's own output in such a document, and it still reads free-text filler leaves.
A generated column that reads a leaf of such a document passes verification when its value is exactly that row's masked leaf, as it does for a document with per-leaf key categories.
SECURITY.md's item 8 states which document columns have every leaf masked and under which category.

94f2809.title: A json document is masked leaf by leaf, each personal leaf by its own category
bullets: A json or jsonb column is now masked leaf by leaf: a leaf with no personal signal, under keys the sampled documents showed, is copied, so configuration documents (model settings, ad-server settings, deployment rules) keep working instead of becoming filler text. On a re-run from a committed lazyslice.yml, only keys the file lists under the column's leaf_keys: entry are copied

Inside a document, a string leaf that holds an email address, phone number, card number, IP address, URL, national identifier, street address or secret, or whose key names such a category, gets a fake of the same kind instead of filler words; the same email masks to the same fake in a leaf and in a text column

A leaf under a key the samples never showed, or in a document with no keys, is still masked, as is every leaf when nothing was sampled; audit, log, history and event tables still replace the whole document with {}

A document column whose own name marks it personal (a jsonb medical_history, masked as special_category on its name alone), or one raised by a yml mask: block or by --mask TABLE.COL=semi_structured, has every leaf masked; that flag is the way to mask personal data under keys no rule knows
Under --phone-region, a national-format phone number inside a document is recognised and masked

A generated column that reads a masked document's leaf, such as Supabase's auth.identities.email, passes verification when its value is its own row's masked leaf, the masker's own fake address; every other post-load check still runs on it

Which keys a column's per-leaf decision covers is the same on every run over the same sample, including when a column shows more than 4,096 distinct keys: keys past that limit, taken in sorted order, count as never sampled, so every leaf under them is masked

README residual 4 and SECURITY item 8 now say that a personal value inside a document is copied when no validator recognises it and no name rule matches its keys (a name under 'attendee', an identity-provider id under 'sub'); the old sentence 'every leaf value is masked' is gone

ee0aa51.title: A go install or a release build uses mask/v0.5.0, whose free_text masker fits its output to the input
bullets: A go install or a release build now masks free text with the v0.5.0 masker: the output is about as long as the input, and exactly as long in a column narrower than nine characters, so a three-value enum-like column and a narrow varchar keep their shape, and the filler fitted to the input leaves out ten state and level words such as trace and default

90ca468.title: The free_text masker fits its output to the input's length
bullets: Columns masked as free text now get a value about as long as the original, not filler of a random length up to the column's width: a role column holding admin, user and guest masks to three short filler words, so state, enum-like and time-zone columns no longer turn into strings of up to 255 characters

Under the same key, a masked free_text value differs from the one v0.3.0 wrote, JSON string leaves included (mask/v0.5.0); the exceptions are an enum or CHECK-list column, a column with an exact-length CHECK and a value longer than its column allows, which mask as before. No other category's masked output changes

Two foreign-key-linked free-text columns of different declared widths (both at least nine characters, or both narrower) now mask a shared value alike and are no longer refused at plan with exit 12 by the equality-group check

A unique free-text column is still refused at plan with exit 12 at every row count, as before; the refusal now reports an admissible domain of 80 (or 21 in a column under nine characters) instead of a width-based figure
SECURITY.md's list of what a snapshot does not hide now names the approximate length of a free-text value beside NULL and the empty string

Case, ligature and ß spellings of one value (STRASSE and straße, file and its ligature spelling) mask to the same output, as they did in v0.3.0, even when the raw values differ in length: the output is fitted to the length of the value's canonical form

The filler a free-text value is fitted from leaves out trace, default, session, level, stage, system, token, value, input and output, words a log_level or settings column is likely to hold itself; a masked value equal to a real value of the same column is what the residual scan stops on at exit 9

6ce191f.title: Commits carry release-note bodies; the tracker and commit skills; make relnotes

9269a7a: A validated foreign key's character columns beside a certain personal column, an email say, are now masked together, instead of both ends being left unmasked whenever one end carried personal data with no other signal to catch it; the walk follows the key upward through every ancestor table, so a chained key three tables deep is masked as a set
A native-script name held as a foreign-key child of a lookup table beside a real email column no longer crosses into the target verbatim
A directly related pair is masked even when a distant lookup table shared through another key could not be masked safely; only the pair's own ancestors decide

When one end of the pair cannot be masked the same way, because it already carries a decision the classifier must not override or is a measured two-letter code lookup, the run refuses at exit 12 before any write, naming both columns with a --unmask escape for each, instead of copying the pair
Masking both ends of a key whose lookup table sits under a small unique index surfaces as the existing exit-12 unique-domain refusal naming both columns
Taking the override on one column of a refused pair is not enough: both have to be accepted explicitly, and the message says so
One real schema in the torture suite, Metabase, needs a second --unmask for a session-id pair whose parent is operator-unmasked while its child is masked; the flag is recorded in the torture suite.
The regression corpus pins the native-script child, the chained key, the blocked-partner pair and the currency-code lookup, whose expected outcome moved to the refusal
db33590: A masker whose output follows the value it was given is now a hard stop rather than a cell the run reports as masked: the mask module refuses it, naming the category and the masker id and never the value.

The two paths that are meant to return a member are still allowed: a masked enum emits one of its own labels, and a generator with a single output (a collapsed special category, the null and fixed maskers, an emptied tsvector) emits its constant.

A masker that panics no longer carries the row out with it: the panic is converted into an error naming the category, the masker id and the type of the panic value, inside the mask module itself, so a program that imports only that module gets the same redaction the CLI does.

A transform refusal no longer prints the masker's own message, which could quote the value it refused; it names the column, the masker and the kind of error, and when the reason is one of the masking module's own — "no masked value fits varchar(8)", "can emit 44700 distinct values" — it names that reason, so an exit-7 refusal is a diagnosis again.
THREAT_MODEL.md T4, T7 and T12 record these three controls as landed rather than owed.

A masked value that happens to equal the value it replaced no longer aborts the run: short-id and birthdate columns, where that coincidence is arithmetic rather than a bug, snapshot normally again instead of stopping at exit 7 with a message about a masker that is not broken.
A masker whose output really does follow its input is still refused, and now so is one that claims a single output to excuse itself.

A jsonb column whose documents are structure only -- {"tags":[]}, {"prefs":{}}, {"a":{"b":{}}} -- no longer stops a run at exit 7 with a passthrough refusal naming semi_structured; a document with no scalar leaf has nothing to mask, so it is copied as-is and the run continues.
A JSON null leaf no longer counts as an unmasked value: {"a":null} passes for the same reason.
A masker that really does hand a document back unchanged is still refused at exit 7 as soon as one document in the column carries a leaf, and the refusal still names only the category and the masker.
2680d5e: A --secret-file whose parent directory is a symbolic link is now refused (exit 5) even on a first run, where the file itself doesn't exist yet to be checked directly — closes the path a symlinked directory component (e.g. a cloud-synced folder) took the masking key out of the repository while the transcript said it had been protected.

A --secret-file that has been hard-linked to a second path is now refused (exit 5, 'secret.refused.hardlink') the same way a world-readable one already was, since a key reachable under a second name may already have been read outside .gitignore's protection.

--password-command is now screened before it is written into lazyslice.yml: a command whose argument looks like a literal value rather than a path (an echo/printf/cat-style command carrying the password itself, most plainly) is withheld from the file and a warning ('secret.password_command.withheld') is printed instead, so the committed yml's 'this file never contains a secret' header stays true.
THREAT_MODEL.md's T5 and T6 sections now document both fixes and their conservative-by-design false-positive tradeoffs.
0395d1c: The container-startup port-mapping race (T-0052) now gets up to 120 seconds of bounded-backoff retry per container, up from 30, before giving up.

If that full 120-second wait is exhausted, the test helper terminates the stuck container and starts a fresh one once, then waits up to 30 more seconds before failing, so a genuinely wedged container fails fast with the T-0052 message rather than pushing a single test binary close to make torture's 60-minute timeout.

The resulting failure message names T-0052 as before, and now also states how long each wait ran and that a restart was attempted, so a torture-suite failure is diagnosable without re-running with -v.

Restarting a wedged Postgres test container after the container never worked no longer risks re-hitting the same stale-reaper crash it was already recovering from: the restart's own container-recreate step now retries once through the same guard the initial container start uses.

A container whose port maps immediately (the common case) is never torn down and restarted; a test pins it so an always-restart bug cannot double make torture's container churn and wall time unnoticed.
112ba1e: Every reference to the maintainer by name in docs, tracker tasks, skills, workflows and the licence now reads "the maintainer"; the copyright holder is Liarea.
Commits from this repository are now authored as Liarea with the GitHub no-reply address.
c621086: A column the run masks can no longer carry an unexplained literal in its own CHECK, generated expression, index predicate, or default that cannot be rewritten -- the plan and the post-load check now refuse it (exit 13) whatever it parses as, not only when a known personal-data shape matches, unless --unmask already names the column, the literal is empty, sits in a closed value list, or is one of the column's own enum labels.

A new value check recognises health, religion, sexual-orientation, ethnicity, trade-union and political-opinion terms in a literal, so a special-category sentence with no digit and no name pair -- for example 'HIV positive, CD4 210' or 'Ahmadiyya Muslim' inside a CHECK constraint -- is now caught and the refusal names the category as 'special_category'.

A SIMILAR TO or NOT SIMILAR TO predicate is now correctly recognised as a pattern rather than a value wherever Postgres writes it back as a call to similar_escape(...), so a Unicode character-class index predicate used for search filtering is no longer mistaken for a personal-data literal and refused.

The refusal message for an unrewritable literal in a masked column's own constraint now reads 'masked column, unrewritable literal in its own constraint' when nothing more specific matched, and still names the specific category (email, address, special_category, etc.) when a recognised shape did.

Two new regression fixtures pin the fix: a special-category sentence in a CHECK on a masked column now refuses at plan, and the same sentence in a CHECK on an unmasked column still refuses with the existing --unmask escape.
THREAT_MODEL.md's account of the special-category DDL-literal rule's history no longer contradicts the amendment describing the current, narrowed scope.
4bfbe36: A masker can no longer smuggle its input value out of the mask module by wrapping one of the module's own sentinel errors (e.g. ErrNoRoom) around it; the error Apply returns now always carries only the module's own safe, value-free text, with errors.Is/errors.As still able to identify the underlying sentinel or NoRoomError/DomainError kind.

A masker can no longer smuggle a value out by forging or rewrapping the module's own *NoRoomError with an attacker-chosen TypeTag string; the caller now always sees the real column's TypeTag/MaxLen, taken from its own Constraints rather than from the masker's returned error.
mask/CLAUDE.md documents the new wrapMaskerError guard and the two attack variants it closes, alongside the existing T-0223 entry.

A masker's DomainError refusal (raised when a unique column's generator cannot mint enough distinct values) now reports the module's own recomputed domain size, required count, row count and max-rows figures, never numbers a third-party masker supplied itself.

No flag, exit code or message format changes: this closes a data-exfiltration channel in the masking library's error handling, where a registered masker could smuggle a few bytes of the value it was asked to mask into a unique-column refusal message via its own Domain() method.
619f23e: A source that is a streaming standby now prints a header line naming it (and, where pg_stat_wal_receiver is readable, its primary's host and port), on every run — not only headless ones.

A headless run (--yes, or no controlling terminal) whose source is a streaming standby and whose --target was not given now refuses at exit 4 naming --target, instead of silently discovering a target that turns out to be the standby's own primary.

The eligibility gate no longer reports a confident "different cluster" when only the source's postmaster start time disagrees and system_identifier could not be read on either side — a standby read against its own primary as the target now correctly prints the "same cluster as source" warning instead of writing with no warning at all.

The recommended read-only role statement printed in the header (and the matching setup guidance) now includes GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION pg_control_system(), which is what lets the strongest cluster-identity check work for this shape.

Documentation only: ARCHITECTURE.md section 9, THREAT_MODEL.md's target-is-production entry and ADR-013 now record the read-replica finding, the fix, and that a live primary-and-standby integration test remains an open gap.

The tradeoff this change carries — a genuinely unrelated target of the same Postgres major reads as "possibly the same cluster" under the recommended read-only role rather than being told apart — is stated in ARCHITECTURE.md and THREAT_MODEL.md and pinned by an integration test, instead of being an undocumented side effect a same-version headless run or CI run could hit with no explanation.

The replica-detection test suite now proves its claims under the same restricted, non-superuser role ARCHITECTURE.md §9 recommends operators create, rather than under the test container's own superuser — closing a gap where the suite could pass for reasons unrelated to what it claimed to test.
45a60bf: A source role denied EXECUTE on pg_postmaster_start_time() (a hardened cluster that also revokes pg_control_system, closing R2-06's original gap) no longer loses its entire cluster identity: the privilege check is now a separate statement sent before the guarded call, so the maintenance-database oid, data_directory and server version still contribute even when the start time cannot be read.

When neither side's cluster identity can be compared at all, the gate now reports the target as possibly on the source's own cluster and prints the 'same cluster as source' warning, instead of silently falling back to comparing the two connection endpoints' spelling -- a comparison guaranteed to disagree for one cluster reached over two transports (a published port and a unix socket, a pooler, an SSH tunnel), which previously let a masked slice land on a production cluster with no warning and exit 0.

Agreement on the maintenance-database oid or the server version alone no longer counts as proof of 'same cluster': both are shared by unrelated clusters built from the same image or PostgreSQL 15+, so agreeing on only those two now reads as unknown (fail-closed) rather than a confident same-cluster warning; disagreement on either still proves the clusters different.

A mid-read failure on the guarded postmaster-start-time field, inside the source's own snapshot transaction, no longer aborts the rest of the cluster-identity read: the read is wrapped in a savepoint so the remaining fields (oid, data_directory, server version) still come back.

New integration test coverage: a source role with EXECUTE denied on pg_postmaster_start_time() still lets the gate recognise an empty, differently-named database reached over a second endpoint as the source's own cluster (the round-3 red-team replay's exact shape), and a forced mid-transaction failure on the guarded field is shown to leave the transaction and the rest of the identity intact.
3466e2f: Every masked first name, last name and full name is now a real, common name from the 2020 U.S. Census lists (958 given names, 1,000 surnames) instead of made-up syllables like 'Bado Bika' or the old list of about 140 names; every masked person name changes in this release, under every key.

Masked email addresses keep their example.com, example.net and example.org hosts, but the given.surname local part now comes from the same Census lists, so every masked email local part changes in this release; every other kind of masked column is unchanged.

A masked name that happens to equal another customer's real name in the same column no longer stops the run: on Pagila's first run (--root public.customer -n 200) 51 first_name and 33 last_name values match another customer's real name, no customer keeps their own, and the run exits 0.
The mask module's exported RoleWords now returns the Census name lists and is due for removal in the next mask minor; importers should stop calling it.
A generated full_name column built from masked first_name and last_name columns loads at exit 0 now that those names are real ones (new regression 041).

SECURITY.md item 12, the README's note on how masked names can match and the README's first-run GIF now describe the Census names; the re-recorded GIF reads back one real name per column and emails such as lance.wells@example.com.

A person-name column too narrow to draw from at least 400 names (for example a varchar(2), varchar(3) or varchar(4) first_name) is refused at plan with exit 12 instead of being masked by swapping between a handful of short names such as Jo and Ty.
A varchar(5) full-name column is masked to a single given name rather than a short given-and-surname pair, because only 22 such pairs fit that width.

49294c4.title: Provisioning passes CI again: the Windows file-mode check and the container readiness deadline on runners are corrected

0fe18ad.title: Discover probe reads inside a read-only transaction; a check that no source statement runs outside one; the read-only prose brought current

a42a130: A previously unreachable rail now catches an unrecognised character column as short as two declared characters (down from sixteen) sitting beside a certain personal column such as email, masking it as free_text instead of copying it verbatim — closing the round-4 red team's native-script varchar(12) leak.
The two-letter ISO-code exclusion (a column whose sampled values are all two-letter codes) is unchanged and still prevents masking of genuine country/language code columns.

A masked column whose generator genuinely cannot write into its declared type still refuses the plan at exit 12 naming the column with the --skip-table and --unmask escapes, exactly as before; nothing new was added for the length case because the existing generator always fits a non-unique column of this shape.

A validated foreign key's short code column (an ISO-style currency or country code, for example) sitting beside an email or other certain personal column is no longer masked on one side of the join while its foreign-key partner stays unmasked on the other, a split that previously died at the load stage's foreign-key VALIDATE step with the target already half loaded; the two ends are decided together, masked as a set or refused at exit 12, as the T-0253 entry says.

Corrected an inaccurate internal explanation of the short-column masking rule that claimed a nonexistent safety net for two-letter codes seen too few times to be checked by value; the actual, correct behaviour (masking such a column when in doubt) is unchanged -- only the documentation was wrong.
b22ebce: A run with no --root flag and no root recorded in lazyslice.yml now asks 'root table? [<top-scoring table>]' at the controlling terminal instead of silently guessing: Enter takes the default, a table name (schema-qualified or bare when unambiguous) takes that table, '?' prints the ranked top five candidates with their score components, and an unrecognised name re-asks with the reason instead of failing the run.

Under --yes, with no controlling terminal, or once discovery has already asked the start/create-target question this run, the root-table question is skipped and the computed default is taken silently, exactly as ADR-008's one-question rule requires.

Whatever decided the root table -- the --root flag, a committed lazyslice.yml, an answer at the prompt, or the computed default -- is now always printed as a decision line ('root public.customers (named by --root) — --root'), the same way the source and target decisions already print.
Three new event codes (plan.root.decided, plan.root.candidate, plan.root.unknown) are documented in docs/ERRORS.md.
README.md's quickstart and docs/QUICKSTART_TRANSCRIPT.md now show the new root-table decision line (verified against a real run) and explain what a run without --root would have asked instead.

Running `lazyslice --tui` with no `--root` now asks the root-table question at most once: the run itself reuses the answer from the preview pass instead of asking a second time and possibly landing on a different table.

Typing a table name at the root-table prompt that matches nothing in the source (including a schema-qualified name, such as a typo'd schema) now re-asks the question immediately instead of accepting it and refusing much later once planning starts.

The table offered as the root-table prompt's default, and any name it accepts, now always matches the table the run actually slices from, even on a schema with partitioned tables, where the two could previously disagree.
A root-table name containing a dot, typed at the interactive prompt, is no longer corrupted before being used to plan the run.
Running the internal/core test suite from an interactive terminal no longer hangs waiting for a root-table prompt nobody can answer.
6478d8f: README now opens with a plain-language paragraph on what lazyslice does and what it refuses to do, instead of jumping straight to a status paragraph.
README gained an Install section: `brew install Liarea/tap/lazyslice`, with build from source as the alternative.

README gained a Quickstart with a transcript that was actually run: the source/target decision lines, the per-column masking reasons, a masked value shown next to its source value, the lazyslice_meta.status = complete marker as evidence of a passing verify, a marker-bound reload, and a same-database refusal at exit 2 - the full untrimmed run is now docs/QUICKSTART_TRANSCRIPT.md.
README gained an 'Exit codes at a glance' one-liner covering every exit code, linked to docs/ERRORS.md for the full table.

README gained a six-sentence safety-model summary: read-only source, an owned empty target held under a lease, deterministic masking under a key that never leaves the machine, every check running before the marker is written complete (and the target emptied on a leak-class failure), and refuse-rather-than-guess as the default.

README's 'What a snapshot will not hide' now lists the five residuals actually accepted after five red-team rounds (row identifiers, an uncorroborated bare national identifier, names in uncovered scripts, any unrecognised shape, and the marker-bound reload window) instead of only the row-identifier quote.

SECURITY.md's known-limitations list gained the same three named residuals (uncorroborated national identifier, uncovered-script names, marker-bound reload window) and corrected the bytea item, which no longer claims bytea is unscanned now that printable text stored as bytea is read like a text column.

README's honesty section on non-Latin-script names now says plainly that the name-matching rules and dictionary are Latin-script only (about twenty languages), so a column named and valued in Cyrillic, CJK, Arabic, Thai, Devanagari or Amharic is not recognised as a name and is masked only when a certain personal neighbour or a foreign-key pair rule catches it, replacing an inverted claim about covering '~20 scripts'.
README's exit-code table now lists exit 1 (an internal failure with no assigned code; run with --debug) and clarifies that the same-database refusal exits 2 at the flag surface rather than exit 4.

README now documents that a Ctrl-C (exit 130) rolls back only the in-flight table's transaction; tables already committed in that run stay loaded, so the target can be left partly loaded rather than untouched.
b4dcbbf: A release now carries checksums.txt.sigstore.json, one keyless Sigstore bundle holding the signature and its certificate, instead of a .sig and .pem pair. cosign v3 writes the bundle by default and ignored the older flags, which is where v0.0.2 failed after building every archive.

Verify a download with cosign verify-blob --bundle checksums.txt.sigstore.json, the identity regexp for this repository and GitHub's OIDC issuer, then check the archive's line in checksums.txt; docs/RUNBOOK.md has the full command.
The orchestrator's own permission to run make tag lives in .claude/settings.json, versioned with the rest of the operating model; it allows that one target and its script and nothing else.
e741bf5: A tag now gets past the release job's setup: the cosign installer action was pinned to a floating v4 that the action does not publish, so v0.0.1 failed before its first step and published nothing. It is pinned to an exact release.
docs/RUNBOOK.md records what broke, how every action a release pins is now checked against its real tags, and that a failed proof is followed by the next v0.0.x rather than a moved tag.
2dce582: README and SECURITY no longer say the 2026-09-09 review's findings are being fixed: they and six red-team rounds have landed, and open work is a GitHub issue rather than a file under tracker/.
772abe6: The same database server reached two ways, a second published port, a proxy, a pooler name or the unix socket, is now recognised as one server: lazyslice refuses it as the source's own cluster instead of dropping its tables

The cluster check reads only values that are the same for every session on a server (its start time in a fixed zone, its version, its data directory when readable, its system identifier when the role may read it) and nothing about the connection it arrived on
A read-only source role and a superuser target still compare: a value one side is not allowed to read is skipped rather than treated as proof of two different servers, so no extra grant is needed

The source's own database, reached on the source's own cluster, is refused even when the two sessions run in different time zones, and still recognised after the server restarted between the two reads, because the system identifier decides on its own wherever both sides can read it
When nothing at all can be compared, a target carrying the source's own database name is still refused rather than admitted

The check is documented honestly: under a SELECT-only source role on PostgreSQL 15 or newer it rests on the postmaster start time and the server version; the maintenance-database oid is the same on every modern cluster
An integration test reaches one container over a second endpoint through a loopback proxy, and a unit test asserts the identity statement reads nothing from the connection
